title: Rails x HotWax
summary:
The meeting focused on preparing additional Shopify shops for rollout, including fulfillment routing, international mappings, accounting treatment, and cutover planning. The team confirmed that routing prioritizes locations within capacity and ultimately allows fallback to the original location by overriding its facility order limit.

Shopify cannot currently reroute orders when the final inventory location cannot fulfill them. HotWax is evaluating either a real-time Shopify POS-to-OMS API call or a Shopify metafield synchronized to the OMS within 10–15 minutes. Until resolved, store teams will route these cases to internal operations for manual queue removal.

Store credit will likely be treated like a gift card and recorded as a credit-memo line item, pending accounting confirmation. Antwerp and the UK pop-up are closed, while Amsterdam remains configured but paused due to staffing. The outlet does not currently fulfill e-commerce orders, but the team recommended retaining its mapping for potential future HotWax use. Canada will continue using HotWax for consistent Shopify-to-NetSuite processing and may require routing that prioritizes Ponyride inventory.

DHL will handle EU and UK shipments, while UPS Worldwide will handle USA shipments. The team will verify international order-sync mappings, including whether gross amount rather than only the rate field should be used. The work involves configuration and access setup, not a software deployment, so downtime is not expected and the existing US flow should remain unaffected.

Because the Labor Day sale continues through September 8 and Canada could receive high order volume, the rollout was moved from September 7–8 to Thursday for all shops. Shopify locations will be activated before cutover. Aggregate locations are unnecessary for shops served by one physical location but should be configured where multiple locations support a shop.
action_items: Cynthia West will review the report provided by the team
Aditya Patel will provide an estimated timeline for the Shopify-to-OMS rerouting solution after the design and implementation approach is confirmed
Jonathan Sew Hoy will confirm the accounting treatment for Shopify store-credit payments with accounting
Gurveen Kaur Bagga will continue mapping the applicable international Shopify fulfillment locations while excluding locations confirmed to be closed
Meeting participant will configure Canada inventory-routing rules that prioritize Ponyride inventory before US/Canada inventory
Gurveen Kaur Bagga will share the shipping and payment mapping sheet for review.
Jonathan Sew Hoy will review how the gross amount field is currently mapped for the Paris order flow.
Gurveen Kaur Bagga will share the Paris Shopify order example for review of the rate and gross amount mapping.
Aditya Patel will activate the Shopify locations ahead of the cutover.
Aditya Patel will follow up on location setup within the next couple of days.
topics: The current routing setup first seeks locations with inventory that remain within capacity and uses a final fallback that overrides capacity limits
HotWax is evaluating a Shopify POS rerouting solution for orders that Shopify cannot natively reroute
Store teams should continue using the internal operations process for manual rerouting until the new solution is available
Store credit is expected to be accounted for similarly to a gift card, pending confirmation from accounting
Antwerp and the UK pop-up location are closed, while Amsterdam remains configured but temporarily paused due to staffing constraints
Canada should use HotWax for Shopify-to-NetSuite integration and may require inventory-priority rules
Anna recommended mapping the outlet shop for inventory processes even though it does not currently fulfill e-commerce orders
DHL is confirmed for EU and UK shipments, while UPS Worldwide is confirmed for the USA.
The team needs to review whether Paris order synchronization should map the gross amount instead of only the rate field.
The cutover is expected to require configuration and access changes rather than a deployment or scheduled downtime.
The cutover was moved to Thursday to avoid changing the Canada configuration during the Labor Day sale.
Shopify locations will be activated ahead of the cutover.
Aggregate locations should be skipped for shops served by one physical location and configured for shops served by multiple locations.
